target.statement: Qwen2.5-VL-3B + SAS retains 68.0% average Hit@1 (99% of dense) with 36.6% FLOPs and 1.44x end-to-end speedup.

compute.basis: The target requires LoRA fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-3B on MMEB (paper uses 8x H100 for Stage I), training the Stage-II exit classifier, and evaluating SAS over 12 retrieval benchmarks, so it cannot be trained or fully evaluated on a normal CPU laptop within hours.

blockers: Stage I uses 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs with LoRA on Qwen2.5-VL-3B
Full 12-benchmark MMEB retrieval evaluation is large and latency/FLOPs measurements assume A100-class GPU execution
SAS training code/configs are only advertised via a GitHub link and are not fully specified in the paper
Reproducing the speedup/FLOPs claim requires reimplementing influence-aware token filtering and adaptive early exit on top of Qwen2.5-VL
title: Skim and Skip: Hierarchical Adaptive Inference for Efficient Multimodal Retrieval
